external_assessments.assessment_scope: 23-account BRICS4CLICKS sample on X during the first month of the Iran war
external_assessments.methodology_summary: ISD analyzed account metadata, repost patterns, naming similarities, reported location/download metadata and shared content. It reported 82% of reposts were in-network and 80% of sampled accounts changed usernames at least once.
external_assessments.caveat: External assessment only. It does not itself create an Atlas behavior class or Hall score. ISD reported no further evidence that the network was state-backed despite amplification by Iranian/Russian state-affiliated accounts.

external_assessments.methodology_summary: ISD analyzed account metadata, repost patterns, naming similarities, reported location/download metadata and shared content. It reported 91% of reposts were in-network; all sampled accounts changed usernames in March 2026.
external_assessments.caveat: External assessment only. It does not itself create an Atlas behavior class or Hall score. ISD reported no further evidence that the network was state-backed despite amplification by Iranian/Russian-aligned actors.

Multiple Iran-war/public-affairs factual-claim surfaces are routed claim-by-claim. WOL-native evidentiary review records six qualifying unsupported/misleading presentation incidents from July 22 through August 6, plus a September 17 31-million-soldiers generalization. Project-owner direct body review additionally reports that Valenti used 'nuclear strike' literally for nuclear-warhead use against Iran and, in the July 27 missile episode, went beyond real interceptor triage to an unsupported motive theory that the U.S. permissively let strikes occur to provoke anger. Those body observations remain explicitly non-transcript provenance until exact captions/timestamps are recovered.

body_capture_queue.title: Trump asked to nuke Iran...
body_capture_queue.research_reason: Determine what request/proposal is actually described in-body, who allegedly asked whom, and whether the title overstates discussion, contingency planning, advocacy, or an actual request.

body_capture_queue.title: Trump CANCELS THE NUCLEAR STRIKE on Iran
body_capture_queue.research_reason: Determine whether the body establishes an authorized/planned nuclear strike that was cancelled, or whether the packaging converts discussion/contingency/rhetoric into an operational event.

project_owner_direct_review.observation: Project owner reports Valenti used 'nuclear strike' literally as nuclear-warhead use against Iran, consistent with his repeated nuclear-armed-aircraft framing, not as shorthand for a conventional strike on nuclear facilities.
project_owner_direct_review.evidentiary_limit: Automated/web retrieval has not recovered captions or timestamps. The already-recorded presentation incident remains independently supportable from the public title plus contemporaneous reporting; this note resolves the intended meaning only at project-review level.

body_capture_queue.title: Trump announces FULL SCALE GROUND INVASION of Iran
body_capture_queue.research_reason: Determine what Trump actually announced versus what the creator inferred from force posture, rhetoric, planning, or third-party commentary.

body_capture_queue.title: Trump sends NUCLEAR ARMED JETS towards Iran.
body_capture_queue.research_reason: Preserve the spoken proposition that the deployed aircraft were armed with nuclear warheads for use against Iran, distinct from mere aircraft nuclear capability or strikes on nuclear facilities.

project_owner_direct_review.observation: Project owner reports Valenti explicitly described aircraft carrying nuclear warheads and framed the deployment as preparation to nuke Iran.
project_owner_direct_review.evidentiary_limit: Automated/web retrieval has not recovered the captions or timestamped spoken text. Do not label this as a machine-captured transcript until exact body wording/timestamps are preserved.

body_capture_queue.title: BREAKING: Trump gives SAUDI ARABIA NUCLEAR WEAPONS
body_capture_queue.research_reason: Determine whether the body alleges literal transfer of nuclear weapons, nuclear-capable systems, extended deterrence, basing, planning, or some other proposition.

body_capture_queue.title: U.S Military ALLOWS IRANIAN MISSILES to hit our bases. Ukraine joins the Iran War.
body_capture_queue.research_reason: Separate the supportable interceptor-triage proposition (commanders may deliberately decline interception of missiles expected to miss valuable targets) from the stronger motive claim that the United States did not care about the strikes / permissively let them occur in order to provoke anger or political reaction.

project_owner_direct_review.observation: Project owner reports Valenti argued the United States essentially did not care, permitted the strikes to occur, and did so to make other actors angry; this is materially stronger than interceptor rationing or threat-based non-interception.
project_owner_direct_review.evidentiary_limit: The public title alone does not prove this motive proposition. Exact transcript wording/timestamps remain required before this body-level motive claim is promoted into a scored WOL-native incident.

research_leads.notes: The exact public handle @zachforthepeople was identified by FOX 9 in 2023 as Zach Metzger, resolving the account identity. Current public searches did not surface material 2026 Iran-war claim activity tied to this handle; absence is bounded to the reviewed public corpus.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline stated that Trump gave Saudi Arabia nuclear weapons.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: BREAKING: Trump gives SAUDI ARABIA NUCLEAR WEAPONS
Publisher promotional short repeats the episode title.
DOE describes a peaceful civil nuclear cooperation agreement and safeguards framework.
Reuters describes civil nuclear cooperation and proliferation concerns, not a weapons transfer.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher title/promo plus contemporaneous U.S. Department of Energy and Reuters coverage of the July 22 U.S.-Saudi nuclear agreement.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The observable factual substrate was a Section 123 civil nuclear cooperation and safeguards agreement. No reviewed source supported transfer of U.S. nuclear weapons to Saudi Arabia.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: The title converts a civil nuclear-cooperation agreement into a literal nuclear-weapons transfer. The underlying agreement is real; the weapons-transfer conclusion is not supported by the reviewed record.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Presentation-level WOL behavior finding. Any canonical proposition about weapons transfer may still be routed to Claims Forensics separately.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Preserve canonical truth adjudication separately from WOL's source-behavior finding.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline stated that Trump sent nuclear-armed jets toward Iran.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Trump sends NUCLEAR ARMED JETS towards Iran.
Public repost preserves the Valenti title and July 23 publication timing.
Contemporaneous analysis says the B-1 bombers heading to the region were no longer nuclear capable and carried conventional weapons.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher headline plus contemporaneous reporting/analysis on the bomber deployment and the aircraft's nuclear status.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The observable deployment involved B-1 bombers. Contemporaneous reporting explicitly identified those aircraft as formerly, not currently, nuclear capable and discussed conventional payloads.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: A real bomber movement was converted into a claim that the aircraft were nuclear armed. No reviewed evidence supported nuclear weapons aboard the deployed aircraft.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Counts the title/presentation claim, not an inference about what the body later said.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Canonical weapon/deployment truth remains upstream; WOL records the unsupported public presentation.

body_review_context.observation: Valenti is reported to have explicitly described the aircraft as carrying nuclear warheads for use against Iran; the proposition is literal nuclear-weapon use, not merely nuclear-capable aircraft.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline presented a Russian missile incursion/crash as 'Russia Bombs Poland.'

public_receipts.text_excerpt: BREAKING: Russia Bombs Poland ...
Publisher promotional short repeats the episode title.
Poland said a Russian missile violated its airspace and crashed, with no reason to believe Poland was the target.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher title/promo and contemporaneous Reuters preservation of Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk's on-site assessment.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The supported substrate is a Russian missile crossing Polish airspace and crashing there during an attack on Ukraine. Poland's prime minister said there was no reason to believe Poland was the target.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: The title upgrades a documented incursion/crash during an attack on Ukraine into 'Russia Bombs Poland.' The attack-on-Poland implication is not supported by the reviewed evidence.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: The Russian origin and Polish impact are preserved as supported substrate; only the attack-on-Poland bridge is scored.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Any canonical NATO/Russia attack proposition remains an upstream truth-adjudication question.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline stated that Trump cancelled a nuclear strike on Iran.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Trump CANCELS THE NUCLEAR STRIKE on Iran
Publisher promotional short repeats the nuclear-strike title.
Reuters reporting describes cancelled massive attacks/strikes, not use of a nuclear weapon.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher title/promo plus contemporaneous Reuters reporting on the attack Trump said he had authorized and then called off.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: Contemporaneous reporting supports that Trump called off planned massive attacks on Iran. The reviewed record did not support a planned nuclear-weapon strike.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: If 'nuclear strike' was intended to mean a strike on nuclear-related targets, the title strips that object qualifier and presents a materially stronger proposition. If it meant nuclear-weapon use, no reviewed evidence supports it. Either reading leaves the public presentation unsupported at the strength stated.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: This is a presentation finding. Body-level narrative remains separately body-gated.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Canonical attack-plan semantics remain upstream; WOL records the unsupported strength of the publisher headline.

body_review_context.observation: Valenti is reported to have used 'nuclear strike' literally to mean nuclear-warhead use against Iran, not a conventional strike on nuclear facilities.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline stated that the U.S. military was out of ammunition.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: BREAKING: The U.S military is OUT OF AMMO!
Reuters reports severe depletion in specific long-range precision missile classes, not zero ammunition across the military.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher headline and contemporaneous Reuters reporting on U.S. ammunition and missile inventories.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: The supported substrate was extreme depletion of ATACMS/PrSM and pressure on other selected munition stocks.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: The title generalizes severe shortages in particular weapon classes into the entire U.S. military being 'out of ammo.' The reviewed evidence does not support that whole-force conclusion.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: A genuine munitions-shortage story is preserved as the substrate; the whole-force zero-inventory generalization is the scored behavior.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Canonical readiness/inventory propositions remain distinct from this source-presentation finding.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline stated that Trump admitted the United States was out of ammunition.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Trump ADMITS the U.S is OUT OF AMMO!
Publisher promotional short repeats the episode title.
Trump said some munition types were tighter but described overall supplies as massive and some as virtually unlimited.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher title/promo and Reuters' August 6 video/transcript of Trump's direct answer about U.S. munitions supply.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: Trump acknowledged some munition types were tighter while saying other types were in very large supply and that overall ammunition holdings were massive.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: The title says Trump admitted the U.S. was out of ammo. The preserved direct statement says the opposite at whole-force level while acknowledging narrower shortages.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Distinct August 6 republication/reframing; not deduplicated with the separate August 4 episode.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Direct quotation semantics support the WOL behavior finding without changing canonical readiness adjudication.

source_behavior_incidents.statement_identity: Publisher headline stated that Iran mobilized 31 million soldiers for a U.S. invasion.

public_receipts.text_excerpt: Iran mobilizes 31 MILLION soldiers for the U.S invasion
AP reports over 600,000 registered for military training, with over one million expected to participate.
The broader campaign was not exclusively military; organizers said 26 percent selected military/security work.
Iranian reporting describes 31 million as campaign registrations/readiness, not 31 million trained soldiers.

evidentiary_support_review.search_scope: Publisher headline, Iranian campaign reporting, AP rally/training reporting, and reporting on the campaign's military versus nonmilitary categories.
evidentiary_support_review.claimant_basis_note: A roughly 31-million campaign registration/readiness claim exists, but the campaign includes nonmilitary roles; contemporaneous military-training registration was reported above 600,000 with more than one million expected.
evidentiary_support_review.search_notes: The title converts a broad and disputed campaign-registration figure into 31 million soldiers mobilized for a U.S. invasion. The factual substrate does not support that conversion.

source_behavior_incidents.downstream_note: Separate September incident; outside the July-August earning cluster but relevant to current source behavior.
source_behavior_incidents.review_reason: Existing canonical training family should atomize registration, training participation, soldier status and invasion framing separately.
